items.description: The Port of Santos is Brazil's busiest seaport and the main maritime gateway for the state of São Paulo. It handles large volumes of coffee, sugar, soy, and container traffic.
facts: Major coffee and soy export hub

items.description: The Port of Paranaguá is one of Brazil's leading agricultural export ports. It plays a major role in shipping soybeans, corn, and other bulk cargo from the south of the country.
The Port of Rio Grande is the main seaport of Rio Grande do Sul and a key gateway for southern Brazil. It supports both industrial cargo and agricultural exports.
The Port of Vitória is a major port complex in Espírito Santo with a strong focus on heavy industry cargo. It is closely tied to iron ore, steel, and cellulose logistics.
facts: Part of a wider port complex

items.description: The Port of Itaqui near São Luís is one of Brazil's deepest seaports and a strategic export point in Maranhão. It serves mineral, grain, and fuel flows from the interior.
The Port of Suape is a major port and industrial complex in Pernambuco, south of Recife. It combines maritime logistics with refining, petrochemical, and industrial activity.
The Port of Pecém is a modern port complex in Ceará that supports trade and heavy industry. It has become an important logistics point for Brazil's northeast coast.
The Port of Rio de Janeiro sits on Guanabara Bay and has long been one of the city's main maritime facilities. It remains important for cargo movement and urban trade.
The Port of Itajaí is one of southern Brazil's main container ports and a key asset for Santa Catarina. It supports regional exports and industrial supply chains.
The Port of São Francisco do Sul is one of Brazil's oldest ports and an important logistics point in Santa Catarina. It continues to handle bulk cargo and export flows on the Atlantic coast.
